summary: Oxford County, ME: 60-foot steel lookout on Mount Zircon, built about 1922; burned and cut down in 1975-76 and left on the summit, where the steel still lies.

facts.status_note: Caught fire in 1975 and was cut down in 1975 or 1976 (sources differ); the fallen steel was left on the summit and a cairn marks the spot

access.note: Hiking trail from a metal gate on a gravel road off South Rumford Road; the land around the spring is owned by the Rumford Water District

visit.trail_note: 2.5-mile out-and-back; the final steep stretch climbs almost 900 feet in half a mile

events.note: Department decides to erect a steel lookout station on the summit; 24, 48 or 60-foot size still open (August 1920 newspaper)
60-foot steel fire tower built on the summit, with a watchman's camp near the gravel road (Maine Trail Finder)
Forest Service fire watchman's camp at Zircon Mountain, per 1924 photo record
Lookout tower cabin rebuilt, per the state biennial report covering 1943-44
Tower caught fire in 1975 (Press Herald); Maine Trail Finder says the camp burned and the tower was cut down in 1975
Tower cut down the year after the fire, and the fallen steel left in place (Press Herald)
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on September 15, 2008; nominated by Bob Spear

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Press Herald says the tower caught fire in 1975 and was cut down in 1976; Maine Trail Finder says the camp burned and the tower was cut down in 1975. The story gives both.
An August 1920 newspaper item puts the planned station on the Milton Plantation/Peru line; a 1924 photo record puts the watchman's camp in Peru. Both are reported.

notes_for_editor: Brief record says 18.3 m, which matches the 60-foot height in the sources; no change needed. Cut-down year conflicts between Press Herald (1976) and Trail Finder (1975); the story reports both. The 1943 event year comes from a report covering 1943-44. The 1920 newspaper quote and 1935 height come from the Forest Lookouts compilation, which quotes newspapers and reports; I did not check the originals. The Press Herald article's publication date was not visible in the cached copy. The Maine Memory record is titled 1924 but its subject line says Milton Twp. and its description says Peru. A hiker forum and a search summary mention a mid-1970s toppling; neither was opened, so they are not used.
